title: What If Humans Never Invented Mirrors?
description:
What if humans never invented mirrors? No reflections. No selfies. No shiny spoons. You're 17 years old and you have NEVER seen your own face — and neither has anyone else on Earth.

In 7 days it's Lantern Night, when everyone hangs a portrait of their own face drawn only from what other people tell them. Your portrait is empty. And 40 years ago, a girl known only as "S." saw her face in a black stone… and has worn a white mask ever since.

If you'd never seen your own face, would you want to? Tell us in the comments 👇

📚 Real facts in this video
• Babies recognize themselves in a mirror only at ~18–24 months — B. Amsterdam, Developmental Psychobiology (1972)
• 1935, Papua New Guinea: "the first time we had seen anything like it" — I. Gershon, Paideuma 54 (2008)
• The first mirrors were polished volcanic glass from Çatalhöyük, ~8,000 years old
• Murano mirror makers were forbidden to leave the island
• A 17th-century French mirror was appraised higher than a Raphael painting
• You prefer your mirror face, your friends prefer the real one — Mita, Dermer & Knight (1977)

This is a hypothetical story for entertainment. The characters are fictional.

title: What If Humans Never Invented Mirrors?
description:
What if humans invented cities, cars, cameras, science, and AI... but never invented mirrors?

In this episode of Invent The Wheel, we ask AI an impossible question and let it build the world that would come from it. A world without mirrors would not only change bathrooms. It would change self-image, fashion, transport, science, privacy, art, and identity.

If there are no bathroom mirrors, people use camera screens. If there are no rear-view mirrors, vehicles become camera-based earlier. If there are no telescope mirrors, science leans harder on lenses, sensors, and computation. And if cameras replace mirrors, seeing yourself may become less private than we think.

The strange lesson: mirrors are invisible technology. They do not only show us what we look like. They give us a private way to meet ourselves.

Question for you: what impossible question should AI answer next?

title: What If Mirrors Never Existed?
description:
Today, Sam will see his own face for the very first time. And it won't be in a mirror.

What if mirrors never existed? No selfies. No checking your teeth. No reflection anywhere. Nobody on Earth has ever seen their own face. Then one morning, someone tells Sam he has a really nice smile... and he has no idea what it looks like.

Every episode of If Not. drops one ordinary person into a world where one modern thing is missing, and follows what happens to their day, their mind, and their life.

title: What If Mirrors Never Existed (You’d Never Know What You Look Like)
description: What if mirrors never existed? You'd still have a face, you'd just have no idea what it looks like. In this video we remove every mirror from history and follow what stops working: the backwards face you only ever see in the glass, the Venetian spies and the 357 mirrors of Versailles, a Halloween candy experiment that shows how a mirror switches on your conscience, a toddler sticker test that suggests your sense of self does not live in the glass, the first rearview mirror at the 1911 Indy 500, and the gold-plated mirror of the James Webb Space Telescope that collects light from more than 13 billion years ago. Research behind the video: Mita, Dermer and Knight, Reversed Facial Images and the Mere-Exposure Hypothesis, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology (1977); Beaman, Klentz, Diener and Svanum, Self-awareness and transgression in children: Two field studies (1979); Broesch, Callaghan, Henrich, Murphy and Rochat, Cultural Variations in Children's Mirror Self-Recognition, Journal of Cross-Cultural Psychology (2011). This is a what-if thought experiment: the studies, dates and figures come from the sources above, and the personal stories are the narrator's own. New videos every week where we delete one thing from history and watch what stops working. Subscribe, and tell us which side of your face you always thought was your good side. #WhatIf #MirrorHistory #Psychology

title: What If Mirrors Never Existed? (You'd Never Know Your Own Face)
description:
For almost all of human history, people had no idea what their own face looked like. No mirrors, no glass, no phones — just other people's reactions telling them who they were.

This video explores the surprising history of mirrors, starting with blurry polished stone and still water, all the way to the first glass mirrors made in 1500s Venice. We dive into Gordon Gallup's famous 1970 mirror test on chimpanzees, which reveals how self-recognition actually develops in the brain. Then we break down psychologist Charles Cooley's "looking-glass self" theory — the idea that your entire sense of identity is built from how other people react to you, not from what you literally see in a mirror.

Even today, with a mirror in every pocket, most of your self-image still comes from other people's reactions, not your own reflection. So how much of "you" is really your own, and how much is borrowed from everyone around you?

title: What Did People Look Like Before Mirrors?
description:
#history #mirrors #ancienthistory Before mirrors, how did people know what their own face looked like? For most of human history… they didn't.

From still ponds and polished volcanic glass to Egyptian bronze, Chinese "magic mirrors", an Aztec mirror owned by Queen Elizabeth I's advisor, and the Venetian secret that France stole — this is the surprising history of how humans first saw their own faces. And stay till the end for the reaction of people who saw their reflection for the first time in the 20th century.
